features.name: Portfolio Diversification Index
features.description: Average pairwise correlation between stocks in the portfolio using equal weights over a rolling window.
features.formula: Let r_{i,t} = daily return of company i on date t. Compute 60-day rolling Pearson correlations ρ_{i,j}(t) between all pairs (i,j). Portfolio metric = mean(ρ_{i,j}(t)) for all i < j

variables.r_{i,t}: Daily return of company i on date t computed from div_adj_close.
variables.ρ_{i,j}(t): Pearson correlation between returns of companies i and j at time t

features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater correlation between stocks (lower diversification), lower values suggest more分散的 returns across the portfolio.

features.name: Market Leadership Concentration Score
features.description: Fraction of total portfolio return contributed by top-performing companies in a rolling window.
features.formula: Let R_t = equal-weight portfolio return on date t. For each day, compute 20-day trailing return for all stocks. Let S_top = sum of absolute returns from top 10% of companies. Metric = S_top / |R_t|

variables.R_t: Equal-weight portfolio return on date t.
variables.S_top: Sum of absolute values of returns from top 10% of companies

features.interpretation: Higher values indicate that a small subset of stocks drives most of the portfolio's performance, lower values suggest more distributed leadership.

features.name: Momentum Shift Frequency
features.description: Count of sign changes in 5-day cumulative momentum over rolling window.
features.formula: Let M_t = 5-day trailing cumulative return of equal-weighted portfolio. Count number of times sign(M_t) ≠ sign(M_{t-1}) within 20-day rolling window

variables.M_t: 5-day trailing cumulative return of equal-weighted portfolio on date t

features.interpretation: Higher values indicate more frequent regime shifts in portfolio momentum behavior.

features.name: Volatility Regime Stability
features.description: Count of volatility crossings above/below 60-day moving average threshold.
features.formula: Let σ_t = 20-day rolling standard deviation of equal-weighted portfolio returns. Count number of times σ_t crosses above or below its 60-day moving average within rolling window

variables.σ_t: 20-day rolling standard deviation of equal-weighted portfolio returns on date t

features.interpretation: Higher values indicate more frequent and unstable volatility regime transitions.

features.name: Portfolio Regime Transition Frequency
features.description: Count of transitions between bull, bear, and sideways market states.
features.formula: Define state_t = 1 if R_{20} > 1%, -1 if R_{20} < -1%, else 0. Count number of times state_t ≠ state_{t-1} within 60-day rolling window
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater frequency of regime changes in portfolio performance patterns.

features.name: Systematic Risk Amplification Index
features.description: Average correlation between individual stock returns and equal-weighted portfolio returns.
features.formula: Compute 20-day rolling Pearson correlations ρ_{i,t} between each stock i's return and R_t. Portfolio metric = mean(ρ_{i,t}) across all stocks

variables.R_t: Equal-weight portfolio return on date t.
variables.ρ_{i,t}: Pearson correlation between company i's returns and portfolio returns at time t

features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater alignment with systemic market factors (higher systematic risk amplification).

features.name: Recovery Velocity Index
features.description: Average number of days required to recover from drawdowns.
features.formula: Identify drawdown periods where cumulative return < previous peak. For each drawdown, compute recovery_days = t - last_peak_date. Portfolio metric = mean(recovery_days) across all identified events

variables.recovery_days: Number of days from drawdown trough to previous peak

features.interpretation: Lower values indicate faster recovery from drawdowns (higher resilience).

features.name: Liquidity Correlation Intensity
features.description: Average pairwise correlation between stocks' dollar volume volatility.
features.formula: Let D_{i,t} = close_i,t × volume_i,t. Compute 20-day rolling standard deviation σ_D,i(t) for each stock. Portfolio metric = mean of Pearson correlations between all pairs (σ_D,i, σ_D,j)

variables.D_{i,t}: Daily dollar volume of company i on date t (close × volume)
variables.σ_D,i(t): 20-day rolling standard deviation of company i's dollar volume

features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater synchronization in liquidity risk across portfolio stocks.

features.name: Sentiment Coherence Score
features.description: Correlation between portfolio returns and cross-sectional volatility of individual stock returns.
features.formula: Compute 20-day rolling standard deviation σ_i(t) for each stock. Compute portfolio metric = Pearson correlation between R_t and mean(σ_i(t)) across all stocks

variables.R_t: Equal-weight portfolio return on date t.
variables.σ_i(t): 20-day rolling standard deviation of company i's returns

features.interpretation: Higher positive values indicate stronger alignment between portfolio returns and market-wide dispersion patterns.

features.name: Risk Contribution Uniformity Index
features.description: Cross-sectional standard deviation of individual stock volatilities.
features.formula: Compute 20-day rolling standard deviation σ_i(t) for each stock. Portfolio metric = cross-sectional standard deviation of {σ_i(t)} across all stocks

variables.σ_i(t): 20-day rolling standard deviation of company i's returns

features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more uniform risk contribution across stocks (better diversification).

features.name: Portfolio Regime Adaptability Index
features.description: Coefficient of variation of portfolio returns during different volatility regimes.
features.formula: Define high/low volatility states based on 60-day rolling σ_t thresholds. Compute CV_high = σ_high / μ_high and CV_low = σ_low / μ_low. Portfolio metric = mean(CV_high, CV_low)

variables.σ_t: 60-day rolling standard deviation of equal-weighted portfolio returns
variables.μ_high: Mean return during high volatility regime
variables.μ_low: Mean return during low volatility regime

features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more consistent performance across different volatility regimes.

features.name: Information Flow Dominance Metric
features.description: R-squared of portfolio returns regressed against trading volume changes.
features.formula: Let ΔV_{i,t} = volume_i,t - volume_i,t-1. Compute portfolio metric = R² from regression of R_t on {ΔV_{i,t}} across all stocks

variables.R_t: Equal-weight portfolio return on date t.
variables.ΔV_{i,t}: 5-day change in trading volume for company i

features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater proportion of price movements explained by trading volume changes (information flow).

features.name: Dynamic Correlation Stability
features.description: Standard deviation of pairwise stock correlations over time.
features.formula: Compute 20-day rolling Pearson correlations ρ_{i,j}(t) between all pairs. Portfolio metric = cross-sectional standard deviation of {ρ_{i,j}(t)} across all pairs

variables.ρ_{i,j}(t): Pearson correlation between returns of companies i and j at time t

features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more stable inter-stock relationships over time.

features.name: Tail Risk Exposure Concentration
features.description: Cross-sectional standard deviation of returns during extreme downside events.
features.formula: Identify days where R_t is in bottom 10% of historical values. Compute cross-sectional standard deviation of {r_{i,t}} on these tail risk days

variables.R_t: Equal-weight portfolio return on date t.
variables.r_{i,t}: Daily return of company i on date t

features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more diversified tail risk exposure across the portfolio.

features.name: Portfolio Entropy of Returns
features.description: Shannon entropy of equal-weighted portfolio return distribution.
features.formula: Estimate probability density function f(R) from 60-day rolling returns. Portfolio metric = -∫f(R)log(f(R))dR
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate more unpredictable/chaotic return patterns, lower values suggest structured behavior.
